  • The AFC cited "substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions" caused by conflicts in the region.
  • Industry observers note that instead of January 7, 2027, the tournament will now kick off on December 23 and end on January 21, 2028.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A little over two months before it was set to kick off, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed its flagship international football tournament in the wake of recent deadly attacks on host country, Saudi Arabia.

The AFC cited "substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions" caused by conflicts in the region.

Industry observers note that instead of January 7, 2027, the tournament will now kick off on December 23 and end on January 21, 2028. The postponement follows delays and cancellations of a number of sporting events in the region, including a Formula One race, the men's and women's tennis finals, the 2027 Dakar Rally and disruption to Asia's marquee continental club football tournament, the AFC Champions League Elite.

Saudi Arabia hosted, and won, the Gulf Cup last month, but there had already been much talk about whether the much larger Asian Cup could go ahead.

It was scheduled to feature 24 teams playing matches in eight venues across Riyadh, Jeddah and Khobar. However, the AFC said that "circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions," made the tournament impossible.

"Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organization and delivery of the competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.".

Industry observers note that in particular, the postponement was forced by a recent wave of deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi rebels as well as other raging conflicts in the region. The Houthis have targeted Saudi infrastructure, including airports. They are fighting a Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognized government, a civil war that reignited in July following a years-long truce.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The AFC had been under pressure from several federations to postpone the tournament, with South Korea's players leading the way.

"The ongoing military tensions and security instability in the Middle East are problems that cannot be taken lightly," Lee Keun-ho, president of the Korea Professional Footballers Association, remarked last month, according to the Yonhap News Agency.

Lee added that "no tournament's value can take precedence over the lives and safety of players and football fans.".

It seems that the AFC now agrees. However, following the announcement of the postponement, Yasser al-Misehal, chairman of the local organizing committee, promised that Saudi Arabia was "fully ready" whenever the tournament ended up being held.

"The tournament will move to the new dates, and our preparations will continue as planned," he told the Saudi Press Agency.

"We're working closely with the AFC and all our partners to make sure the tournament runs smoothly and meets the high standards expected of Saudi Arabia and the Asian Cup.".

Saudi Arabia has invested hugely in sports over the last decade, from owning Premier League teams to hosting boxing title fights and bidding for a number of major sporting events, most notably World Cup 2034, which they won the right to host unopposed.

However, the country has recently withdrawn or slashed funding for a number of sporting events including golf, rugby, tennis and winter sports.

Manchester United have expressed their concern over the circumstances surrounding JJ Gabriel’s imminent move to Real Madrid, and threatened legal action if there is any evidence that he was induced to leave.

The 16-year-old winger posted a video on social media on Tuesday night confirming his departure from United as talks with Madrid continue between his new agent Ali Barat and close family at the club’s Valdebebas headquarters.

United sources say they are disappointed the video appeared without any contact with them, but the club will maintain its policy of not punishing Gabriel for what it sees as the actions of adults.

However, they have reiterated that United will fight with every legal means possible if any evidence of inducement from another club comes to light.

It’s understood that United have been unable to make contact with Gabriel – who has not been seen at the club since September – or his family despite numerous attempts to check on his welfare. They want an opportunity to ensure that he has a say in what could be a life-changing decision.

Gabriel has been training in Madrid and gave an interview to Marca earlier this month saying that he favoured a move to the 15-time European champions over rivals Barcelona, while expressing an ambition to win the Ballon d’Or.

Manchester United are prepared for a legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel.

The youngster is on the verge of joining the Spanish giants in a controversial move.

Sources indicate that he is registered as a United player for the rest of the season and the club are refusing to tear up that agreement in the belief that he would still need approval from FIFA to make the move. However, sources stress that there has been no contact from any football authority seeking to de-register him.

It has been revealed that gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football. He is registered with United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.

There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.

In a farewell post on Instagram he mentioned: 'Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with substantial dreams.

'Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

Recent findings suggest that 'You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

'As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ.'.

Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.

United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered his request to leave given he had become a key part of intends in first team training sessions this season.

United were left rocked in September when Gabriel's family unexpectedly requested to cancel his contract with immediate effect.

Daily Mail Sport revealed at the time that United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered such a move given he had become a key part of looks in first team training sessions this season under Michael Carrick.

A week later, Daily Mail Sport revealed that the decline of United since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson was the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

'His dad has ambitions for his son to be the best in the world and play with the best and learn from the best and right now that's not current situation at United - far from it,' a source explained.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under 21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah.

Industry News: Hull City vs. Brighton: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39.
  • Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.
  • Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39.

Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.

Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.

Conversely, the Seagulls arrive full of confidence after recording consecutive top-flight wins over Manchester City and Brentford, boasting six clean sheets across their last seven league outings.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Hull and Brighton.

Nearly 67 years have passed since Hull City and Brighton & Hove Albion first locked horns - a November 1959 Division Two clash that ended in a 3-1 victory for the Tigers - and there have now been 51 competitive meetings between the two clubs in all competitions.

The Seagulls hold the bragging rights when it comes to overall victories with 22, while Hull have claimed 15 wins of their own and another 14 contests have seen the spoils shared.

Remarkably, none of those 51 encounters have taken place in the Premier League, with every previous battle arriving in the Football League or the FA Cup, and the two sides have not crossed paths since a goalless Championship stalemate in East Yorkshire in February 2016.

Recent clashes between the pair have been notably tight, low-scoring affairs, with none of their last nine meetings across all competitions settled by more than a single goal and three ending 0-0.

During the 2015-16 campaign, both clubs collected a narrow 1-0 victory on home soil - Brighton prevailing in the Championship in September 2015 before Hull gained revenge in the FA Cup four months later - prior to that goalless draw in February.

Indeed, home advantage has heavily dictated this fixture in the modern era, as Hull are unbeaten in their last six home games against Brighton across all competitions - winning four and keeping five clean sheets - since suffering a 2-0 Division Three defeat in October 2000.

Conversely, the Tigers have endured a miserable record on the South Coast, failing to win any of their last 22 visits to Brighton since recording their sole away triumph in this fixture - a 2-1 Division Three success - way back in August 1965.

Brighton built much of their overall head-to-head lead during a dominant spell in the late 1980s and 1990s, rattling off four straight victories between October 1989 and April 1991 before later embarking on a nine-match unbeaten run from April 1993 to December 1996.

That sequence included the Seagulls' biggest-ever win in this matchup, a resounding 4-0 Division Two triumph in March 1996, while they also completed a comfortable league double over Hull with 2-0 and 3-0 victories in the 2000-01 Division Three season.

Hull's most emphatic triumph came in the highest-scoring meeting between the two sides, a 5-2 Division Two victory in December 1988, while they also put three unanswered goals past Brighton in March 1997.

The two teams have also collided five times in the FA Cup, with Brighton winning the first two ties in January 1985 (1-0) and January 1986 (3-2) before Hull turned the tide by edging a 2-1 replay victory in February 2014 following a 1-1 draw and claiming that 1-0 success in January 2016.

Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Recent findings suggest that como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

Sources indicate that the table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

Industry observers note that the absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

The Frenchman has scored 54 goals and provided 61 assists in 122 appearances, although even those phenomenal numbers do not fully reflect what he brings to the Bayern side.

Bayern have reportedly placed a £265m valuation on Olise, who is under contract at the Allianz Arena until 2029.

There is also a significant gap between Olise's earnings and those of Harry Kane at Bayern, and the German club are expected to do everything in their power to convince the winger to sign a new contract.

Industry observers note that "That all said, Bayern Munich have proven that major personal awards like the Ballon d’Or can still be won at FC Bayern. So, that’s the hope of the club and they’ll do everything in their power to keep Olise at the Allianz Arena.".

Olise could still be tempted to stay at Bayern after seeing his club teammate Harry Kane win the Ballon d'Or this year.

A move to a more competitive league could appeal to the Frenchman, while he may also want to join a club where his chances of winning the Champions League are high.

Bayern have not set an asking price for Olise and could demand a staggering fee, with paying such an amount likely to be nothing short of madness.

Arsenal arguably need a right winger who can provide reliable cover for Bukayo Saka rather than a player of Olise's calibre, who would expect to be a guaranteed starter if he made the move to the Emirates Stadium.

Emery has doubts over Matty Cash and Johan Manzambi, who picked up injuries while on international duty and may struggle to recover in time.

  • Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.

  • Sources indicate that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

According to recent reports, juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

Sources indicate that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

Sources indicate that the wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

According to recent reports, the case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, stated it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

According to recent reports, luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

It has been revealed that close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

It has been revealed that the run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

Industry observers note that the first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

If the manager does not explicitly close the door to a new major operation on the transfer market, he insists on the need to maintain a coherent financial strategy, despite Bayern’s ambition to continue to compete with the best European teams.

Herbert Hainer believes in particular that Bayern Munich must compensate for its financial resources lower than those of certain competitors with a more intelligent recruitment policy. “ There are clubs in Europe who simply have more money at their disposal. This is why we must be smarter and better than others “, he continued. To illustrate this strategy, the Bavarian president cited the arrivals of Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Luis Díaz, three operations that were particularly complex to carry out, but which he considers today to be real successes. “ These three players were major challenges to recruit, but they turned out to be real success stories “, he stressed. Hainer also praised the work of CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen, as well as that of Max Eberl and Christoph Freund, who are responsible for the club’s sports policy. A way of reminding us that Bayern intends to continue its development in the long term, without disrupting its strategy for a single European event.

Liverpool maintained their excellent away form by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 before the international break, but Dominik Szoboszlai emerged as an injury worry following the Selhurst Park success.

The midfielder nevertheless joined up with Hungary for the November international break and played the full 90 in both of their Nations League games against Georgia and Northern Ireland, supplying two assists against the former.

Szoboszlai was managing a knee problem during his time with the Magyars, but speaking to the media on Friday, Iraola affirmed that the 26-year-old will be fine for Sunday's main event.

"He's in a good place, he's playing normally, he was not even strapped today so he's fine yes," Iraola responded when asked if Szoboszlai was still being carefully looked after.

As well as confirming Szoboszlai's availability, Iraola delivered positive updates on the Dutch trio of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk.

The latter withdrew from the Netherlands squad for the November window due to an unspecified fitness problem, while Gravenberch and Frimpong were both absent from the win over Palace.

Frimpong sustained a hamstring injury against Brentford in October and has missed Liverpool's last six games in all competitions, while Gravenberch has been dealing with a minor heal fracture.

However, all three are in line to feature against old rivals Man United, as Iraola added: "If everything goes to plan they should be available for the game.

Recent findings suggest that "Gravenberch, it's a matter of pain, he's managing but he's been training the last two days. Jeremie is recovering the same. We've introduced him with the rest of the group, and Virgil is fine to go.".

Should all of Szoboszlai, Van Dijk, Gravenberch and Frimpong make the cut, Liverpool's only remaining concerns are the long-term trio of Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitike.

The latter is still a while away from making a full recovery from an Achilles injury, but Leoni and Bradley have returned to team training as they close in on returns from serious knee injuries.

However, Iraola confirmed that neither defender will be in the squad on Sunday, adding: "The international break was the best moment to introduce them slowly, they've started doing things with the team. They are still not available, but it's very good news and I hope they can play in some weeks.".

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points from their opening 10 games, but they have won just two of their last nine matches against Man Utd.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

"Heartbroken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real." Those were the words with which Spanish second division football club Tenerife confirmed the death of 30-year-old Jesus de Miguel on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that de Miguel was involved in a clash in the middle of the pitch with FC Andorra's Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball with the score 2-2 late in the game. Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.

Spanish media reported that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically" before his death.

After confirming the death on Tuesday morning, the club posted that: "No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news.".

Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" as messages of support began to flood in on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that "I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media.

Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish FA (RFEF).

"Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today," wrote the federation in a statement.

The RFEF postponed Tuesday's matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina, "as a gesture of respect and solidarity.".

De Miguel had been with Tenerife since joining from from Castellon in 2025. He began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023.

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026.

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

In a recent development, 'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'.

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness.

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list.

Industry observers note that joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an crucial part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

In a recent development, post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences.

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

According to recent reports, called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

Recent findings suggest that there were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010).

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

According to recent reports, eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Sources indicate that storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.
  • It is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture.
  • Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.

It is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture. The asterisk signals the inclusion of non-Arab ethnic minorities and people with diverse identities and roots in Southwest Asia and North Africa.

Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.

This year's theme, "Who's Your Diva?!," brought together drag performers paying tribute to legendary figures from across the Eastern Mediterranean who have become queer icons — from Egyptian music legend Umm Kulthum to Turkish star Bülent Ersoy and Lebanese pop icon Haifa Wehbe.

Hassandra, co-founder of ADIRA and the ADIRA Drag Festival, was among the performers, taking on the persona of Lebanese pop star Elissa.

According to recent reports, "It is very vital for me to bring my Lebanese Arab identity and culture into what I do, because I think it's a very beautiful culture. And there's a lot of campy, glamorous, beautiful divas," Hassandra stated.

Industry observers note that elissa's "whole discography is very romantic, raw, soft, kind of like very Adele vibes," Hassandra told DW ahead of the October 30 show. "However, her personality is known to be the extreme opposite. She's very feisty. Very blunt, very unfiltered. Not soft at all as a person.".

Recent findings suggest that the star is also known for speaking out on political issues in Lebanon. She has publicly voiced support for LGBTQ+ communities in the Middle East, while also frequently sparking controversy across the Arab world with her outspoken positions on other political issues.

Hassandra's ADIRA Drag Festival performance addresses this complexity, ultimately "tapping into her sort of controversial political opinions," the drag artist explained.

In a recent development, this reflects one of the ideas Hassandra hopes to promote with the theme of this year's festival. "As queer people, we tend to idealize a lot of pop divas. But these pop divas are very imperfect in their nature," Hassandra remarked. The show provides an opportunity to critically revisit these divas' legacy through a more critical lens.

"And this sort of critical lens can be taken into the outside world, as in: never follow anyone in life blindly. No one should follow any politician, any political party, any pop diva, any activist blindly.".

Recent findings suggest that born in Beirut in 1994, Hassandra studied theater and stage acting at the Lebanese University before moving to Berlin in 2017. "I would say it was it was just a very sort of impulsive decision at the age of 22. I mean, there's no doubt that the economic situation was really bad in Lebanon and continued to become even worse," the artist noted.

Industry observers note that in Berlin, Hassandra became increasingly involved in the city's independent art scene and queer nightlife. Drag emerged as another form of self-expression for the actor.

Through performances that combine theatrical intensity, political humor, grotesque aesthetics and moments of tenderness, Hassandra challenges conventional understandings of gender and identity.

According to recent reports, their work explores themes of home, nostalgia, displacement and queer Arab culture. These ideas are also central to ADIRA, which Hassandra founded in 2023 with Syrian-German DJ and cultural producer Zuher Jazmati, also known as xanax_attax.

Through panel discussions, performances and music events, ADIRA fosters collective participation and community-building.

As Islamophobia and homophobia rise alongside the far right, spaces like ADIRA offer a sense of belonging and support for Arab queer communities.

That sense of community has become even more important following the deadly Islamist terrorist attack during Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride parade in July.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that in the aftermath, Hassandra felt caught between their different identities. As an Arab queer person, "you fall in this position where then you start receiving a lot of racism," they noted.

It has been revealed that "And I think this is why it's crucial, for us queer Arabs, to say we are sad over what happened, but that we also reject any of the racism that comes from that," Hassandra remarked. "I think we [the Arab community] are being used in a lot of ways as a punching bag for a lot of things that are happening.".

Sources indicate that rather than allowing the attack to fuel hatred and racism, Hassandra said, "we should make Germany a safer place for everyone to live in."  "There's place for everyone. It's a huge country," they added.

The interview with Hassandra was conducted by Gönna Ketels.

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 14:21.

Enzo Maresca has provided the latest update on the fitness of his Manchester City squad ahead of Saturday lunchtime’s Premier League clash at home to Fulham.

The Citizens enter this contest seeking to end a three-game losing run, with defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion followed by a 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol both started at the City Ground and were at fault for goal conceded in the first half before coming off at half time due to injury.

While Gvardiol has since recovered from his minor matter and represented Croatia on international duty, Guehi withdrew from the England squad with a hip problem.

However, Guehi was involved in Man City training on Thursday and is set to be available for selection against Fulham.

Clarifying Guehi’s situation following a run of error-strewn performances before his injury, Maresca mentioned at his press conference: “He didn't join internationally because he had a small issue against Forest, but it's not because he needs some break.”.

Fellow centre-back Abdukodir Khusanov pulled out of Uzbekistan duty after sustaining a knock in Man City’s defeat at Forest.

The 22-year-old was absent from all Man City photos and videos from Thursday’s training session and is now a doubt for the visit of Fulham this weekend.

Maresca has also confirmed that Matheus Nunes is a doubt with an unspecified concern; he previously missed three games in October with an ankle issue.

Recent findings suggest that "From the Forest game we still have Matheus (Nunes) and [Khusanov] that are still doubts for tomorrow, because they are still with some problems. We'll see in the next hours.".

The only confirmed injury absentee for Man City is attacker Antoine Semenyo, who is still recovering from a knee injury and is targeting a return next month.

Meanwhile, Maresca has confirmed one guaranteed starter for the match against Fulham, with goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma to continue between the sticks despite a poor run of form.

Donnarumma has kept just four clean sheets in 15 appearances across all competitions this season, conceding 23 goals in total, and his decision making in recent matches has come under question.

According to recent reports, however, Maresca continues to back his fellow Italian, telling reporters: "He has been good. I think with the international team, he made a mistake in the build-up, but for Italy he was the Man of the Match in the game (vs. France), he made many good saves.

"We made some mistakes in the last games. Gigi was part of that. He is aware. Hopefully he's not going to make any more mistakes. He is going to start against Fulham.".

Man City have kept just three clean sheets in their last nine meetings with Fulham, but they have won each of their last 20 head-to-head battles across all competitions – the longest winning run against the same opponent in English football history.

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 14:27.

Tottenham Hotspur have shared footage of Lucas Bergvall and Savio back in training ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town.

The pair have both missed each of Spurs' last four Premier League matches, having picked up injuries ahead of October's 3-1 home victory over Coventry City.

Savio has been dealing with a muscular problem, while Bergvall has been nursing a knee injury, but Roberto De Zerbi expressed hope that the pair would return following the November international break.

On Friday, Spurs posted a 55-second clip on social media showing Savio and Bergvall in training with their teammates, taking part in warm-up exercises and drills with the ball at their feet.

Sávio and Bergvall in training ? ? @Betano_UK https://t.co/3Iug9LlBjf.

De Zerbi then confirmed at his pre-game press conference that the Brazilian attacker and Swedish midfielder are fine to feature against Ipswich, as well as assuring that James Maddison is fit and ready.

However, none of Mykhaylo Mudryk, Tosin Adarabioyo or Mathys Tel will be ready just yet, as the latter is still feeling the effects of the crunching tackle from Jayden Bogle in the 1-0 loss to Leeds United two weekends ago.

"Bergvall, Maddison and Savio are back," De Zerbi mentioned. "Tosin and Mathys Tel no. Tosin is already okay but it is not the right moment to take any risks and Mathys Tel, we need another two or three weeks. Mudryk is not ready yet.".

With Tel sidelined for another two or three weeks, the Frenchman could miss each of Tottenham's next four matches, including the North London derby against Arsenal on December 6.

The Lilywhites will also have to cope without the attacker against Sunderland and Fulham on November 29 and December 3 respectively, and it also remains to be seen if Mudryk will be fit for those clashes after the Chelsea loanee burned bridges with a few Tottenham fans.

In a recent interview, Mudryk reflected on his yearning to join Tottenham's bitter rivals Arsenal in 2024, before Chelsea won the race to sign him from Shakhtar Donetsk.

"Before going to Chelsea, I wanted to join Arsenal. It’s no secret,” Mudryk Ukrainian podcast Guest of Gordon. "Arsenal were the club I wanted to play for, and moving to the Emirates Stadium was my dream.

“There weren’t even any attempts to make my dream come true and move to Arsenal. The attempts from my previous agent were only to earn more money. But at the time, I didn’t know about it. I only understood about the commission and all the rest later on.".

While De Zerbi admitted he could understand Tottenham fans' frustrations, he leapt to the defence of his long-term colleague, adding: "Yes I can understand but Mudryk is a good guy, a good player, he suffered a lot with the situation in the last couple of years. He has to do one thing, show on the pitch his qualities.".

Tottenham head into the weekend in 11th place in the Premier League table, just three points shy of Bournemouth in seventh spot.

CAN 2025: The Senegal-Morocco final replayed?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Frenchfootballweekly

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that could the CAN 2025 final between Senegal and Morocco experience a fresh episode on the pitch?
  • According to recent reports, on January 18, 2026, Senegal won the final against Morocco (1-0), after extra time.
  • Recent findings suggest that can the CAS then decide to replay the match?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that could the CAN 2025 final between Senegal and Morocco experience a fresh episode on the pitch? While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) must deliver its verdict to the “end of November”the hypothesis of a match to be replayed raises questions.

According to recent reports, on January 18, 2026, Senegal won the final against Morocco (1-0), after extra time. But on March 17, the appeal jury of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) finally declared the Teranga Lions forfeited, approving a Moroccan victory with a score of 3-0. A decision contested by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), which appealed to the CAS to recover the title.

Recent findings suggest that can the CAS then decide to replay the match? The body has extensive powers of examination. It can confirm the decision of the CAF, cancel it and render a newly introduced decision, or refer the file to the competent authorities of the African Confederation. It is in particular this last possibility which could, indirectly, open the door to a new meeting. The CAS cannot, however, automatically order that a match be replayed simply because it overturns the contested decision.

A precedent exists. In 2019, after the final return of the African Champions League between Esperance de Tunis and Wydad Casablanca, CAF ordered the match to be replayed. The CAS annulled this decision, considering that the CAF executive committee was not competent, before referring the case to the African football authorities. They then declared Wydad forfeited, a decision finally confirmed by the CAS in September 2020. The match was therefore never replayed.

In a recent development, but the two situations are not identical. The major difference with lies in the facts. Indeed, Wydad refused to resume play after the interruption, while the Senegalese players returned to the pitch and finished the match, winning 1-0. This element could weigh in the TAS analysis.

The possibility that the final of this CAN 2025 will be replayed therefore remains legally possible, but very far from being certain. Especially since the two federations have not publicly requested a new match. After the hearing organized in October, all eyes are now turned towards the end of November, the period at which the CAS must render its decision.

Latest Update: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1048 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.
  • But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
  • The smell of rotten food can make us recoil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.

But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

The smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

Psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

One explanation begins with evolution.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

Sources indicate that but disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:.

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on new experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he stated.

Recent findings suggest that indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe.".

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

"We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar said.

Disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives demonstrated stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

Industry observers note that "A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it.".

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility.".

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he said.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar said.

The upcoming study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

In a recent development, inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best.".

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

"I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he said, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he said.

The research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

Inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he remarked.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics.".

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

It has been revealed that "Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he said. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 14:35.

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly interested in signing Inter Milan midfielder Hakan Calhanoglu.

After enjoying a memorable spell at AC Milan, Calhanoglu switched to their cross-city rivals Inter in the summer of 2021 and has since made 225 appearances across all competitions.

The highly-skilled central midfielder has scored 53 goals and registered 39 assists for Inter, while continuing to impress with his performances this season.

However, his contract situation has cast doubt over his long-term future at the club, with several sides, including Tottenham, reportedly looking to take advantage of the uncertainty.

The Turkish international has a contract at San Siro until 2027, but he is yet to receive an offer to extend his stay.

The 32-year-old wants to continue with Inter, although doing so could require him to accept a significant pay cut, something he is right now unwilling to consider.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, Tottenham are ready to welcome the midfielder, but face competition from Galatasaray, Juventus and Como.

Spurs spent heavily during the summer transfer window to overhaul their midfield, bringing in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes on massive-money deals.

After a nightmare start to the season, Roberto De Zerbi's side are gradually climbing the table and right now sit 11th in the Premier League table with 12 points from 10 matches.

De Zerbi already has plenty of midfield options at his disposal, but it appears he wants a technically gifted and versatile player with proven experience, making Calhanoglu an attractive option.

Calhanoglu operates primarily as a defensive midfielder, although his creative qualities remain a significant asset.

Furthermore, the former Bayer Leverkusen midfielder is renowned for his excellent long-range shooting and could adapt well to the Premier League, even at this stage of his career.

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

On his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

Jackson had been a target for Emery ever since the Basque’s appointment and now has seven goals in claret and blue. It will have been an especially sweet moment for the Senegal forward, for it was Maresca who allowed him to join Bayern Munich on loan while he was in charge at Chelsea.

It has been revealed that city’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

It has been revealed that guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

Maresca said: “I’m not worried about Marc at all, he is playing every game since the season started for us and the national team so it’s not easy. He is ok, it [taking him off] was just a technical decision and like in all games managers make changes. He was on a yellow card and sometimes one yellow card can be dangerous.”.

When asked if the goals were avoidable, Maresca said: “Absolutely, both. Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. We will try again to win at Villa next season. I don’t think we deserved to lose but we learn from that and move on. You can always learn something. For sure there are things we can do better today.”.

While much of the focus will be on City’s 100 per cent start to the league coming to an end, Emery got everything right here. From his team selection to his set-up and substitutions, he outsmarted Maresca on many levels. After the game, Villa defender Matty Cash described his manager as “a tactical genius”.

It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery mentioned: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players revealed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”.

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

Industry observers note that the home team did require Suzuki to produce saves to stop efforts from Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov as City responded. Ndiaye also struck the outside of the post and City were level seven minutes into the second half with Erling Haaland nodding in Ndiaye’s cross at the far post. Haaland had touched the ball just eight times in the opening 45 minutes but invariably only needs one chance.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Industry observers note that enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

It has been revealed that villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Recent findings suggest that emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I was born in North Wales in 1980, and my first memory of football was playing for the school team as a kid.

As a nine or 10-year-old I started getting my cousin’s hand-me-down Everton shirts, and this certainly helped me decide which of the local sides I was going to follow!

The two red sides close by (Wrexham and the other lot) never once turned my head.

Recent findings suggest that and then, in 1991, my mind was made up for good. My uncle asked me if I’d like to go to watch Everton play.

It was the first ever game I’d been to watch live. It was at Bramall Lane, and I’ll never ever forget it.

My uncle got us to the ground early and took me and my cousin to wait for the players’ coach to turn up.

The coach arrived and as I was only a little kid at that point, my uncle lifted me up to get a glimpse of the players.

The first player I saw was significant Neville Southall and I reached over to pat him on the back and wish him good luck. He glanced over his shoulder and gave me a wry smile.

Not only was I now hooked on Everton, but all I wanted to be from that point on was a goalkeeper.

Sources indicate that A few years later I got to taste my first ever trophy win as an Evertonian. Me and my dad watched the whole FA Cup final build-up from Grandstand in the morning to Match of the Day, with the game in between.

We couldn’t get tickets to the final, but my uncle and cousin did go the Charity Shield.

Even though that was my last taste of silverware as an Evertonian, my love for this club has never wavered.

I’m now 46 years old, lived in Australia for 20 years and I’m happily married with seven children – six of which have all been to Goodison and the youngest has beat me to visit the fresh stadium last year!

My highlights of the last 35 years are:.

-              - My first game in 1991.

-              - 1995 and the FA Cup victory.

-              - Going to Howard’s testimonial a few months before leaving for Australia.

-              - Spending a day painting parts of Goodison in 2013.

-              - Goodison trips with my dad, cousins, uncle and taking my six kids to see the eventual champions in 2016.

-              -Taking my two sons to the games in Sydney.

-              - My daughter (who now lives in Rochdale) going to the last game at Goodison.

-              - And my wife taking our two youngest daughters to see our stone at the upcoming ground last year.

I’ve got so many fond memories of our beautiful club, and I can’t wait to make millions more in the coming decades.

It has been revealed that there is no other football club for me or my family. Once a Blue, always a Blue.

My Everton shares first-hand accounts describing the most-treasured memories of fans, players, and staff both past and present.

#2159. Could AI give NFTs a second chance?

Could AI give NFTs a second chance?

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1072 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that remember the NFT boom of 2021?
  • What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.
  • Sources indicate that in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that remember the NFT boom of 2021? The surge in trading of non-fungible tokens (NFTs), which are unique, blockchain-recorded digital assets, was one of the stranger economic offshoots of the COVID-19 pandemic.

What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.

Sources indicate that in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value. The wider cryptocurrency crash was particularly punishing for digital collectibles and largely, they have not recovered.

The sector is worth up to 97% less than it was at its height in January 2022, and sales continue to plummet. So far this year, total global sales of NFTs are less than $2 billion, according to FindWeb3, a cryptocurrency and blockchain jobs platform. That's more than 90% down from the peaks of 2021 and 2022.

In a recent development, does that mean that NFTs will ultimately fade away to nothing, proving right those who dismissed them as a worthless fad? Or is there still some kind of future for them?

In a recent development, "NFTs will still exist, but it will be a niche collectible market," Ben Charoenwong, associate professor of finance at the business school INSEAD, mentioned. "This doesn't mean there cannot be booms here and there, but certainly not take off as people had imagined in the past.".

In a recent development, he thinks whatever future it can have will be "narrow" and notes doubt is growing over the value of "non-fungible" as a concept. Non-fungible means an asset is unique and cannot be traded like for like, whereas fungible means it can be traded like for like, for example, with money.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

He notes that the recent trend of financial institutions converting real-world financial assets, such as bonds and stocks, into digital tokens recorded on a blockchain — the so-called tokenization boom — mostly relates to fungible assets.

However, Andrea Barbon, a finance professor at the University of St Gallen in Switzerland, thinks part of NFTs' future lies in this tokenization boom, as there are some examples of people trading unique real-world assets as NFTs.

Recent findings suggest that "NFT technology is really about ownership," he indicates. "They describe the ownership of a specific asset that could be a digital asset or real-world asset." He says things like real-estate contracts, expensive watches, artworks or luxury sports cars can now be tokenized, with NFTs created to represent these physical objects.

That immediately begs the question: Why would anyone want to have a digital, NFT version of their watch or sports car?

"Some people want to just speculate on the value of the physical asset and for them, it's great that you don't need to move the physical object around," Barbon said.

"If the object is a nice painting and you buy it from the US, you want to ship it to the UK, that's very costly, it's hassle and it's potentially not safe if the value of this painting is very high," he explained.

Sources indicate that he states some companies, such as Courtyard.io, keep physical vaults to hold physical assets which are traded online as NFTs. He says very often, the owner has no interest in having physical possession of the asset.

According to recent reports, another area where he sees some promise for the future of NFTs is connected to artificial intelligence. He states NFTs could help with AI safety, as they could be used to provide unique, verifiable, non-fungible identities for AI agents.

Ethereum and other blockchain providers are in the process of trying to build NFT systems that would represent and verify AI agents, something Barbon says could be very successful.

He envisages a scenario where AI agents are recorded on an NFT blockchain and can then be identified and rated for safety and reliability.

Industry observers note that "Everybody else can then see that the AI agent is actually doing well, you can trust it, it's safe," he states. "In order to do that, you need something which is uniquely attached to each AI agent and that can be an NFT.".

Another possible use he sees for NFTs in the AI era is that writers and artists could tokenize their work as NFTs so that if an AI agent ends up using it for training, the original work can be more easily identified as unique to the creator.

"Maybe you could then claim that the AI organization has to pay you because they have used your content," Barbon says.

While the NFT craze of 2021 can now be seen as a classic bubble, many of those who invested in it have moved on to memecoins and other forms of fungible cryptocurrency, according to Ben Charoenwong.

"Overall, I think the market did not reject blockchains; it rejected non-fungibility," he says.

At the time of the craze, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates stated NFT popularity was "100% based on the greater fool theory," the idea being that one can make money through the purchase of overvalued, fundamentally worthless assets as long as there is a"greater fool" willing to pay even more.

It has been revealed that one of the most famous NFT collections was the Bored Ape Yacht Club, a series of drawings of apes in various locations in various states of boredom. "Obviously, expensive digital images of monkeys are going to improve the world immensely," Gates joked.

Recent findings suggest that in many ways, that collection's current status epitomizes NFTs' fall from grace better than anything else. Although it remains one of the biggest NFT marketplaces, its value has plunged.

The singer Justin Bieber bought one image for 500 ETH (Ethereum), or around $1.3 million dollars. The value fell by around 99% to around $14,000. He still owns it.

Yet the fact that these images still command such prices shows they are not entirely worthless. That offers some hope to those who still believe in the technology. Alongside other possible applications linked to AI and tokenization, NFTs may still have a future, albeit a more modest one than when they first came to public attention.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

It has been revealed that juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he remarked, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

In a recent development, the new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

Sources indicate that the visit highlighted Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

In a recent development, the offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment looks.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Industry observers note that those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

Newcastle United's Amar Dedic has had his bow and arrows taken away from him after causing a major incident earlier this month.

Arteta to meet old foe at St James'.

Both Jaissle and Mikel Arteta will walk suspension tightropes at St James’ Park on Saturday. The Newcastle and Arsenal bosses are on two bookings for the season – and a third means a one-game touchline ban.

When the Spaniard infringed on Sunderland’s managerial area for a third time, referee John Brooks issued a yellow card. Arteta then appeared to sarcastically target Bell with a ‘just tick the box’ gesture.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is a booking away from a one-game touchline ban.

The 2023 match between Newcastle and Arsenal at St James' Park was settled by a controversial winner, with Joelinton accused of a push on Gabriel.

Industry observers note that in another twist, Stuart Attwell will be the VAR this weekend. He was the referee in charge when Newcastle beat Arsenal 1-0 three years ago. The controversial winning goal that night was scored by Anthony Gordon amid suspicion the ball had run out of play before Joe Willock crossed.

Joelinton was then accused by Arsenal of a push on defender Gabriel, while Gordon looked offside. All three incidents survived VAR checks and Attwell’s on-field decision stood.

Arteta was furious and branded the decision an ‘absolute disgrace’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arsenal subsequently issued an official statement backing his criticism and demanded improved refereeing standards. Arteta was charged by the FA over his comments but was eventually cleared.

However, the Premier League's independent Key Match Incidents panel ruled by a 4-1 majority that the goal had correctly been allowed to stand.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are said to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which reveals his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their upcoming deals.

Recent findings suggest that alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing issue for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

In a recent development, slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

He is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.
