📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

Recent findings suggest that in Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

In a recent development, “I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa mentioned. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

According to recent reports, some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Industry observers note that konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has rapidly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

According to recent reports, the victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

Industry observers note that “Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

According to recent reports, “I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

Industry observers note that “We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

Sources indicate that they kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

On bouncing back from defeat...

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

Sources indicate that “Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”.

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz.

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

It has been revealed that arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

Industry observers note that “I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Recent findings suggest that moyes stated: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

Sources indicate that “When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

Sources indicate that his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil declared on Wednesday.

In a recent development, janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

In 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

But luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

Sources indicate that he always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

It has been revealed that janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Industry observers note that janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

There is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

In a recent development, the "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

Recent findings suggest that his iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

Recent findings suggest that guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always remarked that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

It has been revealed that from 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

Recent findings suggest that like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

This article was originally written in German.

Q: Jarrad, it’s still early in the season, but from your perspective, how is it going?

Industry observers note that it’s going well. As a team, we’re in a positive place, especially after the recent results. It’s put us in a good position in the Cup and the Premier League.

Q: With how well it’s going in the league and the Carabao Cup, does it feel like there’s a lot of quality in this Everton squad?

I think the players we’ve got and the quality in the team is probably one of the best we’ve had over the past few seasons.

The squad isn’t as big as other squads, but the quality we have is definitely up there.

I think we’ve just got to stick together and be resilient.

Q: And after recovering from a hamstring injury last season, how are you feeling?

Good. I’m in a good position. I think the summer and pre-season helped to get me where I am now.

I was managed by staff, managed my load through pre-season, managed my training load.

So, hopefully, it’s helping. I'm feeling good.

Q: Just how frustrating was it last season?

Last season was tough. It was the first time I’d had a major injury which kept setting me back. When you can’t find a solution to something, it’s frustrating.

You do everything you can and then it sets you back again.

Recent findings suggest that Q: I remember you breaking down against Liverpool and you looked broken. That must’ve been horrible to deal with?

Yeah, I think it was the fourth time it had happened in the same place.

When you’ve tried different things and nothing’s happening, and then for [the injury] to happen again, it was tough.

Recent findings suggest that it’s probably set me back a bit, so I’m trying to make up for the time I’ve lost. I think the start of the season has definitely helped with that.

Sources indicate that Q: What sort of approach did you take in your recovery? I imagine you tried several options.

I spoke to a few players who’ve had similar issues and reached out to someone in Germany – a specialist there – for a different approach to what I’d been doing, and the Club were on board with it.

I was there for four weeks, and they took me through their procedure, which looked – not just at the hamstring – but how the whole body moves, your brain and how everything moves.

It was a holistic approach and that definitely put me in a better position to come back here, and then with the Club helping me with my load, that put me in a better position.

Q: Are you able to share which other players you spoke to?

Mainly Dominic Calvert-Lewin. When he was here, he was struggling with similar issues, so I reached out to him.

Tom Davies, as well. I reached out to him. They spoke really highly of [the specialist].

I spoke to Merlin (Röhl), and he knew a few people who had been there, so I think it was the right time to get different advice and a different opinion.

Q: But now, you’re feeling in a much better place?

Yeah, I feel in a better position now with the way I’ve been managed, and I feel confident in myself.

I think I feel more confident now coming back and I want to prove to everyone how good I am.

Among the first names on the list is Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens: born in 2004, he made his mark with 17 goals and 12 assists between the ages of 18 and 21 at Borussia Dortmund, before falling through the cracks due to injuries and lackluster performances.

Gittens is going through a tough time at Chelsea, despite the English club’s €56 million investment about a year and a half ago. The 2004-born player has only played 55 minutes this season, which is why he could start elsewhere, far from London.

Neil El Aynaoui has recovered from his injury and is ready to return to action for Leipzig.

The Moroccan midfielder, who left the national team’s training camp early due to leg problems, has received the green light from the German club’s medical staff.

According to BILD, the 2001-born player will be available to Martin Demichelis for the away match against Union Berlin, scheduled for Saturday, November 21st.

El Aynaoui had already resumed partial training with his teammates earlier this week, while sporting director Sebastian Schuppan had ruled out any serious concerns in recent days: “It’s not a serious injury. It’s more of a combination of the games he’s played and the many knocks he’s received. He’s feeling the strain of the last few weeks and months.”.

The international break has therefore allowed him to recover without having to miss further matches against Leipzig.

Industry observers note that the Moroccan has become a regular in Demichelis’s midfield, starting him in twelve of the thirteen matches played so far. His performances have also allowed him to leapfrog Nicolas Seiwald in the Argentine coach’s pecking order.

According to BILD, if he continues at this level, a buyout at the end of the season could become a possibility. Leipzig paid Roma €4 million for the loan of El Aynaoui, with a buyout option set at €25 million.

Before deciding whether to acquire him permanently, however, the German club will also need to evaluate its own financial situation, given UEFA’s requirements regarding transfer revenue.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW noted.
  • Sources indicate that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW noted.

Sources indicate that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the organization sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic said his organization would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have announced plans to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

It has been revealed that it is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has revealed that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler declared on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the organization statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, revealed last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

The January transfer window will soon be upon us, which means a number of clubs will have to decide what to do with their out-of-contract players.

January represents the final chance for clubs to recoup any kind of fee before their players leave on a free in the summer, and there are a number of notable Premier League stars with deals set to expire.

For now, Alisson is leaving in the summer but the goalkeeper has stated publicly he wishes to stay.

He has been at Anfield for eight years, solidifying a previous position of weakness for the club, and has a shout for being the best Premier League goalkeeper of all time.

But he is 34 now and does look less mobile than in earlier years.

He’s on £250k a week, the best-paid goalkeeper in the league, and Liverpool may want to get that off their wage bill but Alisson’s case is helped by the lack of an obvious replacement.

Caoimhin Kelleher was sold to Brentford while Giorgi Mamardashvili has not overly impressed in the chances he has been given.

The Bournemouth stalwart is out of contract this summer having joined 13 years ago.

It has been revealed that the Cherries did have his replacement last season in Alex Jimenez but had to drop their latest signing for off-field concerns. He was loaned to Fiorentina while Bournemouth brought in Juanlu Sanchez but he has played just 18 minutes of football so far.

This has led to 35-year-old Smith being first choice in the team.

The club captain signed a one-year extension last summer but there is right now no talk of another upcoming deal.

Depending on who you believe, Van Dijk is either close to signing a upcoming deal or has one foot out the door.

The Liverpool skipper’s contract expires at the end of the season and no one is 100% sure if either club or player are looking to extend the relationship.

Van Dijk is still a commanding presence in Liverpool’s back line but is 35 now and is on £350k a week, the second-highest wage in the Premier League.

Liverpool would likely offer only another 12 months and so maybe Van Dijk will seek a newly introduced challenge at a club willing to offer him longer.

There are a whole host of centre-backs out of contract in the summer with Dan Burn, Calvin Bassey, Joe Gomez, Fabian Schar, Ben Davies, Michael Keane and Chris Richards all approaching the end but perhaps the most interesting one to watch is Lisandro Martinez.

Having criticised United’s director of football Jason Wilcox over a lack of recruitment, Martinez may well find himself heading out the door to make room for those improvements.

The club do have the option to extend the deal past the summer but are reportedly in two minds about it considering the outburst. The future of the player will likely depend on Mauricio Pochettino’s view of him.

26% of Palace’s squad is out of contract in the summer, which does not seem the best of planning.

One of the most notable is first-choice left-back Tyrick Mitchell, who is reportedly on the radar of Manchester United and Liverpool.

Palace have the option of extending it a further 12 months but are right now in talks to tie him down to a new deal. Failure to do that and Palace could have another Guehi situation on their hands in the near future.

Ayari is coming towards the end of the four-and-a-half-year deal he signed to first join Brighton back in 2023, although the club do have the option to extend it for a further year.

Contract talks over a new deal are not going well apparently, with Ayari yet to commit to anything as he wishes to keep his options open.

The standout performer of the season so far only returned to Brighton in January and penned an 18-month deal with his former club.

That seemed a wise move for a player who will be 36 come the end of it but his current form makes the option of an extension hard to ignore.

If Brighton, who usually have these things planned out, do offer him a newly introduced deal, you suspect it will be for another 12 months rather than committing to a long-term deal for an ageing player.

Europe’s top 10 chance creators in 2026-27: Yamal, Guler, Olise all trail surprise leader.

Fernandes has reportedly already rejected two offers from United but the club do have the right to extend it for a further 12 months.

However, extending the deal of a player who has indicated a desire to leave would not sit well with Fernandes, who has a lot of political capital at Old Trafford.

As for the player, he is 32 now and one League Cup, one FA Cup, one Portuguese Cup and two Portuguese League Cups is not the kind of trophy cabinet that reflects his ability.

He may fancy moving to a different club, one where trophies are more assured, but United look determined to ensure that does not happen until 2028 at the earliest.

Murphy has been at Newcastle for almost 10 years having been signed by Rafa Benitez, which seems a remarkable fact.

His contract is due to expire in the summer with Everton and Nottingham Forest rumoured to be interested, but a loss of many senior players has reportedly prompted Matthias Jaissle to ask the club to keep hold of Murphy.

The Mail claims talks are “accelerating” on a upcoming deal and Murphy, despite being 31, is even being offered improved terms.

Having looked to legally get his contract ripped up in the summer, Mateta will have a much easier route out of Selhurst Park in 2027.

Mateta has been eager to leave Palace for a while now, making it as far as an AC Milan medical before a knee injury collapsed that move.

He is back in the Palace squad now, playing four games this season, but has yet to score and has picked up a red card.

He’s a decent Premier League striker with double digits of goals in the last three seasons but at 29 years of age, he will probably not be sought after by the very top end of clubs.

Mitoma has been on the sidelines since May with a hamstring injury that required surgery.

Understandably, the Seagulls are being careful with his rehab and so it is only this weekend that he is thought to be in contention for the squad.

Pre-injury, Mitoma was one of Brighton’s best players but it feels like the team has evolved a lot since then and there is always a bit of doubt over how a player returns from such a lengthy absence.

His contract expires in the summer and there have been rumours of a departure for two years now, with the Japanese international reportedly wanting Champions League football.

But with his injury, a Champions League club may not want to take the risk and the Seagulls could be in the competition themselves next season.

If he comes back and performs well, it is likely you would expect him to extend beyond the summer.

  • According to recent reports, “He is almost 70 years old.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “He’s right with what he noted I am very demanding of myself and I have to win to be sure of things. This is why I have won so many trophies in my career,” was Jose Mourinho’s humble retort to Claudio Ranieri in the early months of his tenure at Inter.

“Ranieri on the other hand has the mentality of someone who doesn’t need to win.

According to recent reports, “He is almost 70 years old. He has won a Super Cup and another small trophy, and he is too old to change his mentality. He’s old and he hasn’t won anything.”.

Ranieri was in fact only 56 at the time – something that Mourinho almost certainly knew. Now – 16 years later – he is actually 73 if Mourinho feels like a more accurate rehash.

“I studied Italian five hours a day for many months to ensure I could communicate with the players, media and fans,” Mourinho added. “Ranieri had been in England for five years and still struggled to say ‘good morning’ and ‘good afternoon.'”.

While Mourinho was cementing his status as A Special One at Chelsea – doing what his predecessor couldn’t quite manage – by converting Roman Abramovich’s millions into major honours, Ranieri saw his reputation flounder with short and unsuccessful stints in charge of Valencia and Parma.

Still, the Italian was entrusted to take the reigns at newly-promoted Juventus in 2007 following Didier Deschamps’ falling out with the board. He inherited a squad boasting Gianluigi Buffon, Giorgio Chiellini, Pavel Nedved, David Trezeguet and Alessandro Del Piero as the Old Lady looked to rapidly heal the scars of Calciopoli.

Ranieri led Juventus to a respectable third-place finish in their first season back, with a remit to go those couple of steps further as Mourinho – back then the sexiest name in football management – arrived to take the helm at champions Inter in 2008.

Recent findings suggest that juve did make a step forward – second, not third – but the goals had dried up as Trezeguet spent most of the campaign sidelined with a groin injury. Inter had enough about them – with a prime Zlatan Ibrahimovic banging in the goals – to continue their domestic dominance with Mourinho in charge, cruising to a fourth successive Scudetto with a 10-point lead.

Inter’s Portuguese coach was at his spikiest and most self-assured, refusing to shirk away from any verbal battles if he felt slighted by journalists or rival coaches.

Not for the first time, Ranieri found himself in Mourinho’s crosshairs during a wide-ranging rant at the media, Roma, Milan and Juve after a controversial decision to award Mario Balotelli a penalty in a 3-3 draw with Roma.

“There has been the greatest amount of intellectual manipulation. There was a concerted, organised effort to manipulate public opinion. It was fantastic work but it is unrelated to my world – I work in football,” Mourinho claimed as Inter approached the finishing line in 2009.

According to recent reports, “I don’t like intellectual prostitution, I like honesty. Over the last few days nobody has mentioned that Roma have great players but will end the season without a title. Nobody has mentioned that Milan have 11 fewer points than us and will end the season without a title.

“Nobody has spoken about Juventus, who have won so many points thanks to refereeing mistakes. We have only won one game thanks to a mistake and that was the Siena match.

“Ranieri stated he is shoulder to shoulder with Luciano Spalletti? Well, I will side with all the coaches who have fallen foul against Juventus – Cesare Prandelli, Pasquale Marino, Gigi Del Neri.”.

It has been revealed that mourinho responded to the media, Spalleti and Ranieri who accused Mario Balotelli of being a diver, when Inter drew 3-3 with the Spalleti’s Roma. 🤯 pic.twitter.com/u3AeMPpVOs.

— Sir José #Giallorossi (@MourinhoTheGOAT) May 24, 2020.

Ranieri was sacked shortly before the end of the 2008-09 campaign after Juventus went tumbling out of the title race in a run of seven winless matches, while Mourinho signed a contract extension to commit his future at the San Siro.

As Mourinho was gearing up for a second season in charge, a rising Juventus, with Fabio Cannavaro making an ill-fated return following three years at the Bernabeu, were still being talked up as Inter’s likeliest challengers. Carlo Ancelotti and Kaka had left Milan, while Roma finished a distant sixth.

Luciano Spaletti had led Roma to the Supercoppa and Coppa Italia, as well a runner-up finish in Serie A, during the 2007-08 season, but they struggled to maintain the same standards the following year. After Roma started the 2009-10 season with back-to-back defeats to Genoa and Juve, Spaletti resigned.

After a summer off, Ranieri promptly found himself back in a job – at his hometown club, who he’d grown up supporting. But few if any pundits expected Roma to seriously compete with the journeyman coach at the helm – not least Mourinho, who evidently didn’t consider Ranieri a rival, every passing mention dripping with patronising contempt.

“Everyone knows that Ranieri is not a top-class coach, but he will not be expected to win the Scudetto. The target at the moment is middle-tier, so Roma have gone for a middle-tier coach,” wrote GOAL Italia’s editor Sergio Stanco in an op-ed reacting to the appointment.

And when the Giallorossi lost three Serie A matches in a row in late October in a series of fraught battles full of bookings and red cards, Roma found themselves down in 14th, two points clear of the relegation zone.

The only question was whether they could salvage a Europa League place, let alone mount a title push – Inter had started the season like a train and were 14 points clear after 10 matches.

What happened next, against all the odds, was one of the most thrilling and hard-fought title races that European football has ever seen.

READ: Comparing Claudio Ranieri’s eight best teams: Fiorentina, Chelsea, Leicester….

Sources indicate that slowly but surely, Ranieri’s Roma began to find form, holding table-topping Inter to a 1-1 draw at the San Siro as they kicked off a 24-match unbeaten run. Come to the winter break, they were up to fourth – but 11 points behind Mourinho’s league leaders.

In the fresh year, Roma began to mix dazzling performances with gritty 1-0 wins. They looked like a title-winning side. Mirko Vucinic and Francesco Totti were routinely producing match-winning displays, while Daniele De Rossi was at the peak of his powers, looking every bit a world-class midfielder.

Recent findings suggest that ranieri’s men took 40 of the first 48 points available, winning 12 and drawing four, following the winter break. All the while Juventus were plummeting down to midtable obscurity since their decision to dismiss him.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Inter were faltering. Their comfortable lead was getting whittled away. They failed to win back-to-back matches between January and April and were constantly dropping points on their travels, failing to win at Bari, Parma, Napoli, Catania, Palermo and Fiorentina.

In a recent development, come late March, and their visit to the Stadio Olimpico, Inter’s season looked on the verge of complete collapse. Mourinho’s man for the moment Diego Milito cancelled out De Rossi’s early opener, but Luca Toni – during a memorable half-season loan from Bayern Munich – came up with an iconic match-winner that resulted in one of the loudest roars in the history of the Eternal City. No Gladiator could muster a moment like this.

Sources indicate that FLASHBACK | 💥 | On this day in 2010… a classic finish from Luca Toni secured victory against Inter Milan! 👋#ASRoma pic.twitter.com/NjMdSyLaQs.

— AS Roma English (@ASRomaEN) March 27, 2018.

Recent findings suggest that all season, Ranieri had played down his side’s chances of doing the impossible, just as he’d done at Juventus and just as he’d do at Leicester. But once Roma moved within a point of the top spot with seven games to go, the tinkerman allowed himself to dream.

“We’re out of the last bend and now we are on the final straight, one metre behind Inter,” remarked Ranieri after their 2-1 victory over Inter.

“We have reopened the title race, now it will be a test of nerves. For five months we have chased and sacrificed ourselves to the cause; now we have beaten a stratospheric team who deserve our compliments.”.

An early Europa League exit to Panathinaikos at the first knockout hurdle allowed Roma to focus on domestic matters, while Inter were going deep into the Champions League.

Not only did the Giallorossi stand in Inter’s way in Serie A – even briefly usurping them to the top spot in April, with five games to go – but they were also their opponents in the Coppa Italia final.

But it was at this point, with their backs to the wall and in stark danger of crashing and burning, that Mourinho’s Inter did what the truly great sides do and stood up to produce some of their greatest performances when they needed to.

The counter-attacking masterclasses served to Barcelona and Bayern Munich in the semis and final of the Champions League were their most famous victories, but they were pushed to be every bit as good back home as the league and cup went down to the wire.

Milito, as he so often did in the defining games at the business end of Inter’s historic treble, came up with the decisive intervention and notched the only goal of the game in the Coppa final at the Olimpico, while a frustrated Totti was shown red in the dying moments.

After going top with three points against Atalanta, Ranieri’s Roma held onto their place at the summit the following week in a full-blooded derby against Lazio, peppered by 12 yellow cards and one red but most importantly a 2-1 win.

But a week later they succumbed to a 2-1 defeat at home to Sampdoria. Totti had given Roma an early lead, but a second-half brace from Giampaolo Pazzini was enough to blow their title hopes. Just as you’d be brave to mention Steven Gerrard’s slip in the red half of Merseyside, Pazzini is a name best avoided in Rome.

Sources indicate that iconic image of Mexes crying on the Roma bench was 10 years ago today. The infamous Roma-Samp pazzini game. The game that cost Roma the scudetto #ASRoma pic.twitter.com/R6yfaxo4eW.

— Scot Munroe (@scot_munroe) April 25, 2020.

In a recent development, it was Roma’s only defeat of their last 28 in Serie A, while they won eight of the last nine, but it was enough to cost them. Inter took advantage by winning their last five in a row, taking 19 of 21 points on offer after their defeat in the capital.

History is written by the victors, after all, leaving Roma to be remembered as one of the great nearly sides and Ranieri destined to be a nearly man – until Leicester, of course.

It was Ranieri’s miracle Foxes, after all, that inflicted a 2-1 victory on Mourinho’s Chelsea in December 2015, keeping them at the top of the table and their opponents just a point above the relegation zone.

Mourinho was then sacked, but – water under the bridge, apparently – he revealed support to Ranieri following his dismissal at the King Power the following year, wearing CR on his training top in his press conference.

In a recent development, ranieri returned to Roma for an emergency two-month spell at the end of the 2018-19 season. “Mr. Ranieri, in our moment of dire need, you have answered. Now, you receive the homage of your people,” read one banner and the veteran coach struggled to hold back the tears on the touchline in his first game back in charge at the Olimpico.

He later returned for a third stint, once again in their hour of need during the 2024-25 campaign.

Industry observers note that mourinho has since done something Ranieri never quite could and delivered silverware for the Giallorossi. But he never quite surpassed the love the Eternal City has for one of its favourite sons.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.
  • Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

If left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'.

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23.

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

“Last year’s comeback against Parma was crucial; it opened the doors to the Champions League for us. It was a fundamental step. This upcoming season is different; the objectives are emerging along the way.”.

Recent findings suggest that on the strength of the squad, despite the many absences. “We’ve had strong performances from other players, which have helped us avoid feeling the impact of the absences. There are still a lot of games to go, and players who aren’t playing can play more, or vice versa. We’re in constant conversation with D’Amico, but there’s been no transfer planning other than between the two of us.”.

According to recent reports, midfielder Carlos Baleba and striker Benjamin Sesko remain out for the foreseeable future with their injuries. Marcus Rashford is still a doubt as well, but isn’t too far off a comeback.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Well-known former Chelsea, Barcelona and Liverpool players are among the big names to have retired in 2026.
  • Time is a curse for a football fan, as a host of players we have watched for major periods of their career call it a day and hang up their boots.
  • We’ve looked into 18 players who have called it a day in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Well-known former Chelsea, Barcelona and Liverpool players are among the big names to have retired in 2026.

Time is a curse for a football fan, as a host of players we have watched for major periods of their career call it a day and hang up their boots.

We’ve looked into 18 players who have called it a day in 2026.

Berahino has retired from football at 33 to concentrate on his role as a coach with Burundi’s national team.

It feels like a long time ago that he scored 20 goals in league and cup for West Brom in 2014-15. That made Berahino hot property, with Spurs seriously keen before plumping for Son Heung-min instead.

The striker never did capture that form again, faltering with the Baggies before a disastrous £12 million move to Stoke in 2017.

Berhaino has since played for Charlton and Sheffield Wednesday, before spells in Cyprus, India and Slovenia.

Pedro ends his playing career as one of the most decorated players in modern football, having won the World Cup and Euros with Spain alongside a plethora of trophies at club level.

The forward was part of Pep Guardiola’s glittering Barcelona side, before scoring 43 goals in 206 Chelsea appearances.

He left to join Roma in 2020, before becoming the first player since 1985 to move between the two Rome rivals when he signed for Lazio in the following year.

Pedro remained at Lazio until his decision to retire at the age of 39.

After a glittering career, including World Cup glory in 2014 and 49 goals for Germany, Podolski called it a day in May 2026.

The 40-year-old represented several European giants throughout his career, including Bayern Munich, Inter Milan, Galatasaray and Arsenal.

He ended his career with boyhood club Gornik Zabrze in Poland and even skippered them to cup glory in his final campaign.

Borini played for Chelsea and Liverpool in the early-2010s, but is still beloved at Sunderland for his relegation-dodging goals under Gus Poyet and Sam Allardyce.

The forward left Wearside in 2018, spending time in exotic locations like Milan, deepest Turkey and Salford. He retired in October 2026.

Former Arsenal, Swansea and West Ham goalkeeper Fabianski has hung up his gloves at the age of 41.

But Fabianski has no intention of quitting the game entirely, announcing his intends to work with the next generation of goalkeepers in a coaching role.

No Premier League player has ever made more appearances than Milner, who broke Gareth Barry’s long-standing record in February 2026.

The midfielder made his Leeds debut in 2002, sharing a pitch with sepia-toned names like Nigel Winterburn and Lucas Radebe.

His career with Leeds, Aston Villa, Newcastle, Manchester City, Liverpool, Brighton and England was nothing less than stellar and Milner called it a day this year at the age of 40.

started his career at Cardiff City before a 2008 move to Arsenal, where he won three FA Cups – scoring the winning goal in two of those finals – during his 11 years with the Gunners.

He then had spells with Juventus, Nice, Rangers, a second stint at Cardiff and Pumas UNAM before ending his career in April.

Ramsey is now manager of League One side Oxford United.

One of the biggest sh*thouses in recent football history, Costa was a menace during his days with Atletico Madrid and Chelsea.

He played his last professional match in 2024, but it wasn’t until earlier this year when he appeared on a podcast that he confirmed his retirement.

Oscar was just 25 when he signed for Shanghai Port, leaving Chelsea for a £60million fee and plenty of raised eyebrows.

The Brazilian spent seven years in China to the glee of his bank manager, although a player of such talent should really have been playing in a more competitive league.

In a recent development, he spent the last few months of his career at Sao Paulo, before retiring in April. This was due to a heart condition which led to him collapsing and requiring CPR in a training session.

Young brought the curtain down on an exceptional 23-year career in May, retiring at the age of 40 after a final season with Ipswich Town in the Championship.

Starting as a winger with Watford and Aston Villa, Young gradually became a defender during his Manchester United days and won a Serie A title with Inter Milan in 2021.

He was also an key member of England’s 2018 World Cup squad.

One of the biggest ‘Streets Won’t Forget’ footballers in Premier League history after his spell at West Ham in the mid-2010s, Payet retired earlier this year.

Sources indicate that the French playmaker spent the final years of his playing days at Vasco de Gama, still capable of scoring outrageous free-kicks. A maverick in an increasingly systemised sport.

Most famously associated with Leicester’s 2016 title win, Schmeichel retired in May 2026 after suffering a shoulder injury a few months previously.

Then with Celtic, it was expected that Schemeichel’s surgery would keep him out of action for up to a year anyway.

Aged 39, the son of legendary goalkeeper Peter enjoyed a hugely successful career in his own right.

A loyal servant at Chelsea between 2012 and 2023, Azpilicueta ended his career in May after helping Sevilla avoid relegation.

The full-back made over 500 appearances for Chelsea, the sixth most in the club’s history, and appeared as a BBC pundit during the World Cup.

An eight-times capped Netherlands international, Van Ginkel represented big clubs like Chelsea and AC Milan, but his careers at both clubs were short.

In England, he also played for Stoke, but the midfielder featured in his home country for the majority of his career, playing more than 100 games for both PSV Eindhoven and Vitesse.

At 33 years of age, Van Ginkel has hung up his boots.

Pjanic had a very successful career at club level, playing for giants such as Roma, Juventus and Barcelona.

The Bosnian won seven trophies with Juve, one with Barca and was named Roma’s footballer of the year in 2014.

At international level, he’ll go down as a legend, having represented his country over 100 times, while he contributed to two goals in his three World Cup games.

It has been revealed that pjanic technically retired in the final days of 2025, but who cares for such semantics? Any excuse for us to relive his glory days at Lyon.

Sakho left Paris Saint-Germain for a Liverpool team which wasn’t particularly good while he was there, and in doing so ended his spell of winning trophies: four at PSG and not a single one in his career after that.

The Reds finished second in Sakho’s first campaign there, before slipping to sixth and then eighth in the Premier League for the following two seasons.

Sakho was on the club’s books as they finished fourth the next season, though he was on loan at Crystal Palace when that happened.

He would move permanently to Palace, netting Liverpool a healthy fee, then back to France with Montpellier, before his final spell in professional football with Torpedo Kutaisi in Georgia.

Mata finished his career playing in Australia, leaving Melbourne Victory in September before confirming his retirement in November.

The Spaniard starred for Chelsea and Manchester United in the Premier League in his prime after coming through the Real Madrid academy and making his name at Valencia.

A World Cup winner with Spain in 2010 and a member of their triumphant Euro 2012 squad, Mata is now bowing out at the age of 38.

A three-time Europa League winner with Sevilla, Banega was clearly eager not to just be remembered as the guy who ran over his own foot at a petrol station.

The midfielder had a 10-year international career with Argentina and was most recently playing back in his homeland with Defensa y Justicia.

But at the age of 38, he’s saying enough is enough. “Even if Messi calls me for Inter Miami, I would tell him no,” insisted Banega, who also noted he wouldn’t want to “take the place” of young players trying to break through at clubs.

José Mourinho hasn’t budged on Endrick’s future, having long been in Roma’s sights as a way to strengthen their attack in the January transfer window.

Sources indicate that speaking at a press conference on the eve of the match against Celta Vigo, the former Giallorossi coach reiterated his desire to keep the Brazilian at Real Madrid, despite rumors of a possible departure: “I need him. I love Endrick, and Real Madrid is more important than him. This means we need him to stay here.”.

The message was also addressed to the 2006-born player’s entourage and to clubs interested in his signing, with Mourinho further clarifying his position: “My response to the agents, to the newspapers… is this: I need Endrick, and therefore Real Madrid.”.

It has been revealed that the coach’s position, however, doesn’t completely rule out a possible departure in January, considering that Mourinho himself has acknowledged the management’s decision-making power: “If the club’s higher-ups decide otherwise, I will respect it. But I want him to stay here 100%.”.

Roma continues to closely monitor the Brazilian’s situation, having been identified as one of Gasperini’s potential reinforcements for the January transfer window.

6 times players came back to haunt their old club ahead of Bruno Guimaraes’ Newcastle return

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Guimaraes is the latest Premier League player to return to a former club as Arsenal take on Newcastle United, but will the Brazilian follow in the footsteps of others and get a goal?
  • From apologising to full-length runs of the pitch, players scoring against their old clubs results in a number of different reactions.
  • Here are six of the best of them from Premier League history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Guimaraes is the latest Premier League player to return to a former club as Arsenal take on Newcastle United, but will the Brazilian follow in the footsteps of others and get a goal?

From apologising to full-length runs of the pitch, players scoring against their old clubs results in a number of different reactions.

Here are six of the best of them from Premier League history.

We’re generally against players not celebrating goals against former clubs but when that player has played 648 times for them, perhaps we can understand it.

Lampard’s move from Chelsea to New York City came with an unexpected stopping-over point of Manchester City where of course he scored against his former club.

It was at the Etihad and City were trailing thanks to a goal from Andre Schurrle when Lampard scored an equaliser five minutes from time.

He looked like a dog that had just eaten something he knows he shouldn’t have as he put a single hand up in the air to apologise.

Rooney’s departure from Everton was a little messy with Everton fans chanting against him even as he was still their player and that bitterness was still there three years later.

In 2007, United trailed Everton 2-0 which gave the home fans the confidence to give their old player a bit of stick.

According to recent reports, but it was a case of kicking the bear. United levelled in the 68th minute after Phil Neville put the ball in his own net and 11 minutes from time, Rooney grabbed the winner.

And there was certainly no lack of a celebration.

After a few bounces like a man who could not decide what to do, Rooney looked the Goodison Park faithful in the eye and kissed the United badge.

Would Wayne Rooney have worked in Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona?

It is the absolute gold standard of blood-boiling celebrations.

Adebayor was annoyed at Arsenal for what he felt was Arsene Wenger forcing him out, resulting in a £25.5m move to Manchester City.

Wenger suggested it was more a need to raise money but Adebayor took it to heart and let his emotions come out when the two clubs next met.

He netted in a 4-2 win and sprinted the full length of the pitch to taunt the travelling Arsenal fans. Referee Mark Clattenburg looked like a disappointed parent while stewards struggled to hold the enraged Arsenal fans back.

In a recent development, it was not Adebayor’s only moment of the game either. He stamped on Robin van Persie’s face, landing him a retrospective three-match ban, and even got into arguments with Cesc Fabregas and Alex Song.

Ince had controversially made his way to Liverpool having previously spent six years at United and he rubbed salt into the wound in 1999.

A few weeks before United would go on to lift the treble, Ince scored a late equaliser at Anfield and celebrated by hugging about six different fans in the stands.

The goal and result looked to have swung the title race to Arsenal but United did eventually lift the trophy.

Van Persie was enemy number one around the Emirates in 2012 after he left for Manchester United and he acknowledged that fact when he scored in the first three minutes when they met at Old Trafford in the 2012/13 season.

He gave a double-handed apology and looked genuinely disheartened by the goal. In the away leg, he scored once more but again refused to celebrate.

Six months on though and Van Persie very much did celebrate.

He rose well to meet a Wayne Rooney corner and went full knee slide in his celebration. As he was hugging Rooney, his face did though look like a man who’s just remembered he was supposed to not celebrate.

It’s not one of the more well-known names but we are including it because it led to a rule change.

LuaLua was on loan at Portsmouth from Newcastle at a time when there was no restriction on when loan players could feature.

Newcastle were winning 1-0 away at Fratton Park when guess who scored to equalise it. Bearing in mind he was still an employee at this point, LuaLua celebrated by taking his shirt off in what is possibly the furthest thing away from an apology.

Newcastle manager Bobby Robson mentioned: “He was the last player we wanted to score against us. One of our players has taken a point off us.”.

That bizarre situation led to the Premier League tweaking the rules to prevent loaned players from facing their parent club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On November 20, 2010, Tottenham Hotspur played their part in one of the most memorable North London derbies in history with a 3-2 comeback victory over Arsenal. How well do you remember that side?

In a recent development, to jog your memory: goals from Samir Nasri and Marouane Chamakh (of all people) gave the Gunners a two-goal lead within the opening half an hour. But Spurs raced back with three second-half goals to register their first win away at Arsenal in 17 years.

“I gave them a rollicking at half-time, and woke them up a bit,” Harry Redknapp said afterwards.

In a recent development, “We took the game to them from the start of the second half. We had to go for broke. It wasn’t a case of trying to stem the tide, it was a case of trying to get back into the game.

“We were either going to get beat 5-0, or have a go. That’s what we did, because that’s my nature.”.

He added: “We can beat anybody. This has put us right back in the race again. It’s wide open. “If my players believe in themselves as much as I do, we can achieve anything.”.

Spurs went on to finish fifth but that shouldn’t detract from a famous victory at the Emirates.

According to recent reports, we’re asking you to name the 11 players that Redknapp chose in his starting line-up that afternoon. The time to beat from the Planet Football office is 01:34 but any Spurs fans worth their salt will fancy their chances of beating us.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, said.

Sources indicate that “We got on the front foot and demonstrated our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the upcoming campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

It has been revealed that tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back rapidly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” noted Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

In a recent development, kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".
  • It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".
  • Shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".

It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".

Shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns. In last Friday's ruling, the CAS stated that the IIHF's concerns were "not supported by sufficient evidence.".

Wednesday's statement comes after two days of talks by the IIHF Council aimed at charting a way forward following Friday's CAS decision, which appears to have caught most of the international ice hockey community off guard.

In a recent development, two of the organizing committees the statement refers to are those of Canada, which is due to host the IIHF World Junior Championship starting next month, and Germany, which is to host the IIHF Men's World Championship next May. Both countries are strong supporters of Ukraine in its war against Russia, and both have expressed serious reservations about their upcoming tournaments in light of the CAS ruling.

On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ruled out allowing Russians to compete in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he told reporters at a press conference in Antigua, where he was attending a Commonwealth meeting.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

Last weekend, Frank Lutz, chairman of the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) conceded in a television interview that following the CAS decision, the DEB would "also have to consider the option of handing back (hosting rights to) this championship.".

In a statement to DW on Wednesday, a German government spokesperson reiterated Berlin's position on the matter from the weekend, saying it viewed Friday's CAS ruling "very critically.".

The spokesperson also stated  the government would "consult with the German Ice Hockey Federation in the near future regarding the potential consequences of this decision, including its impact on the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany.".

Meanwhile, the ice hockey association of Finland, the defending men's world champions, has been spearheading an effort to boycott upcoming IIHF tournaments should the Russians be allowed to compete.

"We are currently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen said in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Czechia have since made similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson stated.

This came shortly after Norway noted it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

"Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors.

Czechia Ice Hockey Association President Alois Hadamczik confirmed on Tuesday that they too would refrain from playing Russian teams.

Latvia's federation said it “reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

Alexander Helwig, chairman of the Austrian Ice Hockey Association told public broadcaster ORF that “as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia.".

USA Hockey has yet to comment on the CAS ruling.

At the same time, sponsors of IIHF tournaments are also getting cold feet. Skoda, which has been the main sponsor of the Men's World Championship for more than three decades, told the Associated Press that it would "reassess" its position if Russia takes part.

Sources indicate that "We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions. With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld," the Czech carmaker noted.

Skoda isn't alone either, Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian had noted it would end its backing if Russia took part and Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, whose logo has been seen on the boards and officials' jerseys at World Championships since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

On Wednesday afternoon, yet another sponsor joined the list, with German workwear tech giant Strauss saying it would "forgo all logo exposure associated with the (men's) tournament" and was considering withdrawing its sponsporship entirely.

With the IIHF Council having failed to agree on how to proceed during its meetings on Monday and Tuesday, President Franz Reindl told Germany's SID news agency on Wednesday, that it would reconvene for further talks on Thursday.

This article was originally published on November 4, 2026. It was updated on November 5, 2026 with the German government statement to DW.

Everton tasted their first defeat in the Subway Players Cup as the Blues' four-game winning streak in the competition came to its conclusion with a 2-1 defeat away to Manchester United.

First half strikes from Mared Griffiths and Emma Watson put the Red Devils in to a two-goal lead, before Noemie Mouchon halved the deficit two minutes after the break.

Prior to Wednesday night's clash, the Toffees had comfortably beaten Birmingham City, Newcastle United and Sheffield United before thrashing Durham 6-0 in the competition.

Head coach Scott Phelan named a heavily-rotated XI from the side that were held to a goalless draw against Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.

Rylee Foster-Inman started in between the sticks, with Issy Hobson making her first appearance in two months in front of her.

Up top, Mouchon led the line after netting a brace in the Blues’ 6-0 demolition of Durham seven days ago.

According to recent reports, foster-Inman produced a fine save when faced one-on-one with Griffiths inside six minutes. The keeper rushed out upon recognising the danger and did brilliantly to narrow the angle.

The shot-stopper denied Griffiths once more on 21 minutes as the youngster pulled the trigger from the edge of the box after a cute turn saw her evade Hobson.

The lively Griffiths was in the thick of the action once more in the 34th minute as United came inches away from opening the scoring. Rebecca Bernal burst forward to meet her in swinging cross, the Mexican’s header sailing just over.

It has been revealed that griffiths would not be denied only 60 seconds later as the forward broke the deadlock in style. She sprinted down the left before chopping past Finnigan and firing past the outrushed Foster-Inman.

Watson then doubled the hosts’ lead on the stroke of half-time. Ella Toone wrong-footed Finnigan before pulling it back to the former-Blue. Watson finished emphatically from close range, with that concluding the action for the opening 45.

Defensive duo Hobson and Silcock made way for Hannah Blundell and Rion Ishikawa at the break.

Everton halved the deficit only 60 seconds after the restart as Mouchon netted her third goal from her last two Cup appearances. Quick feet from Vignola allowed the Spaniard room to free Hannah Cain down the right. The Wales international then squared it to the advancing Mouchon, who finished off the post.

Recent findings suggest that maz Pacheco then came agonisingly close from 20-yards out as her wicked free-kick rattled the upright. The full-back picked her spot from the set-piece – the ball crashing against the crossbar with the keeper well-beaten.

Phelan then made two further changes on 68 minutes as Ruby Mace and Hikaru Kitagawa replaced Clare Wheeler and Vignola.

With eight minutes remaining, Naomi Layzell – who claimed the Player of the Match award when the two sides met in the WSL – came on in place of Aurora Galli.

Despite a late push for an equaliser, United stood firm and succumbed the Toffees to their first defeat in the Subway Players Cup.

Everton return to Goodison Park on Sunday afternoon (2pm KO) as Brighton & Hove Albion travel to L4.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s new home or at least they will when everything is in order.
